claims.text: US President Donald Trump announced a binding deal with Denmark to give Washington permanent control over Greenland's security and bar Russian and Chinese military bases from the territory.
Denmark and Greenland stated that any security deal with the United States would not compromise Greenland's sovereignty.
Denmark and Greenland plan to sign the security agreement with the United States next week at the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen stated in a social media post that a binding agreement would strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic while respecting Denmark's red lines.
Donald Trump has repeatedly insisted since returning to the White House in January 2025 that Washington needed control over Greenland for strategic reasons.
Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen stated that the security agreement recognizes Greenland's interests and benefits everyone.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated that the deal is great for NATO and Europe because it strengthens common security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.
A US State Department official stated that the deal guarantees China and Russia cannot send troops, host a base, or make investments in sensitive sectors in Greenland.
Donald Trump's pressure campaign for control over Greenland began in December 2024 after he won re-election.
In his early 2025 State of the Union address, Donald Trump stated that the United States would get Greenland one way or another.
Several European militaries previously deployed a multinational naval mission to Greenland to assess security threats.
Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the Greenland agreement comes at no cost to the United States.
A NATO spokesperson stated that the military alliance welcomed the Greenland security deal.
An unnamed US State Department official stated that the security agreement would not expire even if Greenland becomes an independent country in the future.
An unnamed US State Department official stated that the agreement grants the US unilateral power to build additional military structures without approval from Greenland or Denmark.
The United States permanently stations more than 100 military personnel at its Pituffik base in northwestern Greenland under a 1951 agreement.
Greenland has a population of roughly 56,000 residents.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the agreement a historic deal and a huge win for the United States.
More than two-thirds of Greenland's territory lies within the Arctic Circle.
Donald Trump stated that US presidents had known the strategic importance of Greenland for more than 100 years, but none had been able to address it.
Donald Trump first floated the idea of purchasing Greenland from Denmark in 2019 during his first term as president.
On January 9, Donald Trump stated that the United States could use military force to seize Greenland.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen warned in January that a US invasion of Greenland would end NATO.
Saudi coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki stated that Saudi air defences intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh at dawn on Saturday.
Saudi coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki stated that air defences thwarted Houthi attempts to target civilian infrastructure in Bisha, Taif, Farasan, and Yanbu.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree stated that the group targeted sensitive sites in Riyadh and an Aramco oil facility in Yanbu with cruise missiles, ballistic missiles, and drones.
Yemeni government armed forces reported killing 12 Houthi fighters during an infiltration attempt in southern Marib.
Yemeni government forces reported that 13 soldiers were killed in two days of clashes with Houthi forces in Taiz and Lahj.
A column of black smoke rose near Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport following Houthi missile and drone strikes.
Clashes between Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces on Saturday resulted in 48 deaths according to military sources quoted by AFP.
The International Organization for Migration reported that recent fighting in Yemen has displaced more than 104,796 people.
The Houthis recently seized control of Mokha port and Perim Island in the Bab al-Mandab strait.
Saudi Civil Defence issued overnight alerts warning residents in Riyadh and Al-Kharj of a hostile aerial threat around 3 a.m.
Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei stated that Tehran wants the Saudi-Houthi war to end and believes the Yemeni side also wants a settlement.
The United States approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia.
The United Nations reported that nearly 3,000 people have crossed the sea to Djibouti due to renewed fighting in Yemen.
Saudi Civil Defence sent phone alerts overnight on Friday warning residents of potential aerial attacks in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Yanbu.
The UN Security Council issued a statement condemning continued Houthi attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and their military escalation in Yemen.
The Houthis recently took control of the Red Sea islands of Greater and Lesser Hanish.
Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei stated that Tehran formally conveyed seven conditions to Washington via Qatari mediators to end the war.
Mohsen Rezaei stated that Iran's conditions for ending the war include an end to hostilities on all fronts, the release of frozen funds, and an end to the naval blockade.
Mohsen Rezaei stated that Iran changed its military planning to focus on US naval assets in the Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and Arabian Sea.
Mohsen Rezaei claimed Iran recently test-fired a multi-warhead anti-ship missile near a US vessel or aircraft carrier.
US President Donald Trump told Axios he was facing a big decision over whether to resume major military action against Iran.
US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth launched his Send Me Tour in Texas using the biblical words Whom shall I send.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's net favourability rating dropped to a record low of -24 points amid public frustration over the war in Iran.
The cost of hiring a large crude carrier to move oil from the Persian Gulf to China crossed $1 million per day for the first time, reaching $1.035 million per day.
Insurance premiums for shipping vessels in the Persian Gulf rose to about 10% of asset value aboard, up from 0.5% to 1% before the war.
Diesel prices crossed $6 per gallon for the first time, standing about 60% higher than before the war in Iran.
Mediators Qatar and Pakistan have been working to restart negotiations between Washington and Tehran since their previous memorandum of understanding expired.
Former Pentagon official David Des Roches stated that Iran appears to have dropped its previous demand for war reparations in its latest terms sent to Washington.
Mohsen Rezaei denied Iranian involvement in Yemen's war and stated that closing the Bab al-Mandeb Strait is a Yemeni matter tied to the Houthis.
US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that he will form an AI Force and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar.
Donald Trump stated on social media that AI is the next Industrial Revolution and could account for as much as 25% of US GDP.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for industry-wide deceleration, regulation, and independent monitoring of AI model development.
The UK Parliament Joint Committee on Human Rights published a report calling for a new bill on AI to address human rights risks.
Donald Trump stated that calls to slow down AI development are a hoax generated by the Radical Left Dumocrats.
California Governor Gavin Newsom announced plans for a panel to develop AI safety regulations, including a potential kill switch for rogue AI programs.
Donald Trump proposed calling artificial intelligence Superior Intelligence, Extreme Intelligence, or Supreme Intelligence instead.
Donald Trump compared his planned AI Force to his creation of the Space Force during his first presidential term.
Former AI tsar David Sacks resigned earlier this year and currently serves as an external adviser and chair of Trump's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
The US House of Representatives passed a bill 417 to 3 to minimize the impact of AI data centres' electricity consumption on consumer utility bills.
Donald Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House on September 24, with AI expected to be among the topics discussed.
Secret Service officers deactivated and confiscated press credentials for journalists from MS NOW, CNN, and Politico on Saturday morning.
Donald Trump announced on Friday that he was barring CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House, accusing them of reporting fiction and lies.
White House Correspondents' Association President Jacqui Heinrich called on the Trump administration to immediately restore access for the banned journalists.
MS NOW reporter Akayla Gardner and CNN reporter Betsy Klein were denied entry to the White House on Saturday morning after their badges failed to scan.
Politico reporter Cheyenne Haslett was denied entry to the White House complex and had her access pass confiscated by Secret Service.
The 1977 federal appeals court decision Sherrill v. Knight established that the White House cannot deny press access arbitrarily once press facilities are established.
In 2025, the Trump administration restricted Associated Press access after the news agency declined to adopt the administration's preferred name, Gulf of America, for the Gulf of Mexico.
The New York Times issued a statement calling Donald Trump's ban of CNN, MS NOW, and Politico an unconstitutional threat and expressing support for the targeted news outlets.
MS NOW announced on social media that it intends to take all steps necessary to defend its First Amendment rights against the White House ban.
